# Marilla Cuthbert

## Overview

- **Age:** Middle-aged  <sub>[v1 c3 P0](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0000)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c3 P0](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** Managing the Green Gables household  <sub>[v1 c6 P29](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0029)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss Cuthbert  <sub>[v1 c6 P14](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0014)</sub>; Miss Marilla Cuthbert  <sub>[v1 c19 P90](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0090)</sub>

## Appearance

Marilla is a gaunt woman with graying hair and sharp angles. Though initially described with a grim expression, her face softens over time as her dynamic with Anne matures.

_Sources: [v1 c3 P12](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0012), [v1 c33 P15](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0015)_

## Personality

Marilla possesses a practical, unsympathetic, and brisk exterior, strongly valuing order, duty, and plain sense over imagination. Despite her stern demeanor and tendency to reprove others, she harbors a deep capacity for moral responsibility, pity, and underlying affection.

_Sources: [v1 c3 P0](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0000), [v1 c3 P20](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0020), [v1 c6 P19](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0019), [v1 c6 P26](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0026), [v1 c26 P26](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0026)_

## Traits

- Practical and unsympathetic to nonsense  <sub>[v1 c3 P20](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0020)</sub>
- Brisk and stern  <sub>[v1 c3 P0](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0000), [v1 c6 P27](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0027)</sub>
- Responsible and compassionate under a hard exterior  <sub>[v1 c6 P19](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0019)</sub>

## Abilities

- Managing household chores and farm tasks such as milking cows  <sub>[v1 c6 P29](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0029), [v1 c26 P26](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0026)</sub>

## Goals

- Bring up Anne properly and instruct her in discipline and practical work  <sub>[v1 c19 P90](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0090), [v1 c26 P26](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0026)</sub>

## History

Marilla Cuthbert arranged alongside her brother Matthew to adopt an orphan boy to help on their farm at Green Gables. Due to a misunderstanding, Mrs. Spencer brought an eleven-year-old girl named Anne Shirley instead. Though initially shocked and intent on resolving the mix-up, Marilla was moved by pity and a reluctance to hand Anne over to the harsh Mrs. Blewett. After consulting with Matthew, Marilla decided to keep Anne at Green Gables to bring her up properly. Over time, she managed Anne's upbringing with strict discipline while secretly taking pride in her growth, appearance, and accomplishments. She also developed a warm, quiet tolerance for Anne's imaginative outbursts and social friendships.

_Sources: [v1 c3 P0](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0000), [v1 c3 P4](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0004), [v1 c6 P14](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0014), [v1 c6 P19](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0019), [v1 c6 P20](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0020), [v1 c19 P90](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0090), [v1 c19 P93](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0093), [v1 c33 P17](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0017), [v1 c33 P18](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0018)_

## Background by volume

- Lived at Green Gables with her brother Matthew Cuthbert  <sub>[v1 c3 P1](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0001), [v1 c6 P29](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0029)</sub>

## Quotes

> Matthew Cuthbert, who’s that? Where is the boy?  <sub>[v1 c3 P1](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0001)</sub>

> Well, don’t cry any more. We’re not going to turn you out-of-doors tonight. You’ll have to stay here until we investigate this affair. What’s your name?  <sub>[v1 c3 P13](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0013)</sub>

> Unromantic fiddlesticks! Anne is a real good plain sensible name. You’ve no need to be ashamed of it.  <sub>[v1 c3 P20](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0020)</sub>

> I think you’d better learn to control that imagination of yours, Anne, if you can’t distinguish between what is real and what isn’t.  <sub>[v1 c6 P24](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0024)</sub>

> The way I feel at present, Anne, is that it’s high time you had those dishes washed. You’ve taken half an hour longer than you should with all your chattering. Learn to work first and talk afterwards.  <sub>[v1 c26 P26](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0026)</sub>
